task: GitHub issue #19 (epic #27): extend the Wave 8 sequential external-driver round trip into an agent-executable bridge — a ready/claim/submit lifecycle (ClaimLedger-style claim semantics on top of the event store, new EventType INVOCATION_CLAIMED) so an external agent can execute Tikhon invocations without holding the event store: ready renders the next TaskEnvelope and records a fencing claim, fresh claims fence a second driver, stale claims are re-issued with attempt+1 and the old token rejects, submit validates the claim token then commits through the unchanged Wave 8 coordinator machinery

acceptance.criterion: tikhon ready --db PATH --run-id ID prints the next ready invocation as a TaskEnvelope JSON (superset/reuse of next) and marks it CLAIMED via a new EventType INVOCATION_CLAIMED (claim token uuid4 hex, claimed_at UTC, envelope digest); a claimed-but-unsubmitted invocation is NOT handed out again by a subsequent ready while the claim is fresh
acceptance.evidence: src/tikhon/bridge.py ClaimBridge.ready renders via ExternalDriver.next_envelope (Wave 8 reuse) then appends INVOCATION_CLAIMED (EventType added additively in src/tikhon/runtime/events.py); fresh-claim handouts return {"ready": false, "claim": ...} with nothing appended. tests/test_bridge.py::test_ready_records_claim_event_with_token_digest_and_attempt (token/digest/claimant/attempt on the event), test_fresh_claim_is_not_handed_out_twice (ready=false, same token, zero new events) and the CLI demo artifact fenced-second-ready.json prove it.

acceptance.criterion: Stale claims: a claim older than --claim-timeout (default 900) is dead; ready re-issues it (new claim token, attempt+1) and the old token then rejects; the attempt counter persists in the envelope/claim events
acceptance.evidence: On re-issue ClaimBridge._issue_claim appends a fresh INVOCATION_DISPATCHED (same binding) so the re-rendered envelope carries attempt+1, then INVOCATION_CLAIMED with a new token and claim_attempt+1 (persisted in both the event payload/attempt column and the handed-out envelope). tests/test_bridge.py::test_stale_claim_is_reissued_with_new_token_and_attempt proves claim_attempt=2, envelope attempt=2, two DISPATCHED events, old token rejected (claim token mismatch) AND old echoed attempt rejected (Wave 8 stale attempt check), with nothing appended by either rejection.

protocol_deviations: The issue body's fuller surface (heartbeat/renew of a live claim, stdin input for large envelopes, dedicated documented exit codes beyond the CLI's existing 0/1 convention) was descoped to the orchestrator's required ready/claim/submit lifecycle: renewal is covered by the expiry + re-issue semantics instead (an expired claim gets a fresh token and attempt; there is no extend-in-place), and large envelopes already travel by --result-file. Existing CLI conventions (structured JSON on stdout, 'error: ...' + exit 1 on stderr) are reused rather than a new exit-code table.

Re-issue fencing is implemented by appending a fresh INVOCATION_DISPATCHED (same binding) before the new INVOCATION_CLAIMED so the envelope attempt increments and the old envelope's echoed attempt rejects through Wave 8's attempt == len(dispatched) check — rather than bumping only a claim-local counter. This keeps one attempt notion across envelope and claim events, at the cost of a second DISPATCHED event per re-issue (intentional: at-least-once dispatch).

submit with an expired-but-not-yet-re-issued token is rejected (fencing): a dead claim cannot submit even if no one else took the work; the invocation becomes available again at the next ready. A submit WITHOUT --claim-token keeps the exact Wave 8 behavior, so a claim-less/coordinator-driven run is unaffected; on a claimed run this legacy path is still guarded by the Wave 8 attempt/duplicate checks.

The external driver (hence the bridge) supports plain sequential DO steps only; IF conditionals and CALL expansions are rejected up front with a clear DriverError, inherited unchanged from the Wave 8 ExternalDriver.

The task brief said 'all 22 registered commands'; the builtin registry does expose 22 commands (via PYTHONPATH=src; a stale non-editable site-packages copy exposes only 17, the known issue-18 workaround). program.think uses six of the 22 (define, search, extract, summarize, check, verify); every command in it is registered and lint reports valid.

A first demo session attempt hit my own session-script sequencing bug (fencing demo placed after the claim was already settled); the run.db was reset and the session re-run clean from scratch — the committed artifacts are all from the single clean pass.
